extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers of comedy/Norm Macdonald
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and analyzing the attributes, techniques, and professional considerations of Norm Macdonald's comedy (stand-up, talk-show appearances, and TV satire). Useful for writers, performers, and students of comedic style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan delivery, eccentric understatement, folksy turns of phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Style characterized by deadpan delivery, eccentric understatement, and the use of folksy, old-fashioned turns of phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead description of Macdonald's comic voice — implies that effective material for this style should be delivered flatly, with understatement and colloquial/old-fashioned language rather than overt emoting. Example contexts: stand-up routines, talk-show appearances, observational bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaotic yet understated comedic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Developed a reputation for his chaotic yet understated comedic style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine elements of apparent disorder or unpredictability (chaos) with an overall restrained or low-key delivery (understatement). Use juxtaposition between content and delivery to create surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running jokes and non-sequitur punchlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent use of running jokes and non-sequitur punchlines (e.g., repeatedly referencing Frank Stallone as an absurd punchline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: build recurring callbacks or an unrelated recurring name/image to create absurdity. Anti-pattern: overuse that becomes stale or provokes real-world complaints (stopped after Sylvester Stallone's request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set expectations then subvert (pull the rug out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedic technique of setting audience expectations and then pulling the rug out from under them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a setup that leads the audience in one interpretive direction, then deliver an unexpected twist or reversal. The National Post and other critics described this as a hallmark of Macdonald's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimalist/deadpan stage persona ('no opinions')
rubrics_metrics.description: Later-career shift to a more reserved deadpan style in which Macdonald claimed to have 'no opinions', reducing gesture and verbiage to an absurd minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance strategy: minimize physicality and verbal elaboration; let timing and phrasing carry the joke. Works for material that benefits from implied absurdity rather than explicit commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target selection — avoid 'low-hanging fruit'
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressed distaste for the 'low-hanging fruit' of easy political targets (explicitly mentioned Donald Trump jokes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle: prefer more original or challenging targets/angles rather than obvious, overused political hits. This affects both perceived craft and critical reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation and impressions as homage
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief stated that imitation is the highest form of flattery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for performers doing impressions: framing impressions as homage/tribute can be a stylistic choice and affect audience reception; Macdonald frequently performed impressions (Larry King, Burt Reynolds, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your subject when attacking religion or large institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: While judging, Macdonald criticised a contestant: 'If you're going to take on an entire religion, you should at least know what you're talking about.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for satirists: ensure factual or cultural familiarity before lampooning religions or broad institutions to avoid shallow or ill-informed jokes that invite criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-audience-pleasing, uncompromising material can be a deliberate choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Macdonald admitted his 'Update was not an audience-pleasing, warm kind of thing' and that he did jokes he knew wouldn't get larger reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic stance: choosing material that may not maximize immediate audience applause can be valid if aiming for a particular voice or long-term critical reputation. Trade-off: networks/programs concerned about ratings may react negatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context sensitivity and institutional constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Networks and producers may remove or sanction material considered inappropriate or damaging to ratings — e.g., removal from Weekend Update allegedly related to O. J. Simpson jokes and ratings concerns; producers' personal relationships can influence decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consideration: TV performers must be aware of producers' sensitivities, corporate relationships, and ratings data; controversial material risks censorship, firing, or ad bans (Dirty Work ads incident).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversial subject anti-patterns and repercussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes about violent crime, sexual violence, or victims (e.g., John Lotter / Brandon Teena comment) can provoke activist backlash, threats of picketing, and public apology/retrospective removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid casually making light of victims or violent crime without clear satirical framing; be prepared for organized backlash and institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone choice in roast or ensemble contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: At the Comedy Central Roast of Bob Saget, Macdonald performed intentionally cheesy, G-rated material that contrasted with raunchier roasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate tonal contrast can be an effective strategy in ensemble formats — choosing a different register (clean/cheesy) can make material stand out, but must fit the performer's persona and the event's dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when to stop a recurring gag when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Macdonald stopped Frank Stallone jokes after a 1997 request from Sylvester Stallone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/professional guideline: pay attention to requests from subjects or rights-holders and to limits of mockery; continuing despite clear requests can create unnecessary conflict or loss of opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of autobiographical or semi-fictionalized material
rubrics_metrics.description: Macdonald authored a semi-fictional novel 'Based on a True Story' that presented a heavily fictionalized account of his life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blending fact and fiction in memoir/comedy writing, make the boundary and intent clear (e.g., 'not a memoir') to manage audience expectations and legal/ethical risks.
